samples.summary: Unrequested scope: a whole peer-writable-numeric hardening program (fontSize / lineHeight / cell padding / image size bands, `row-height.ts`, and a new `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` bound inside `paginateLayout`) is bundled into the #1050 list-subtree fix. The task file `docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md` scopes the change to `planListLevelChanges` + threading `siblings` + (in review follow-ups) `normalizeListLevel` at the raw readers; nothing in the plan or the follow-ups covers row heights, font sizes, line heights, cell padding, image sizes or a page-span cap. It is not merely additive either: out-of-band values now read as *absent* (e.g. an inline image with an edge > `MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` is dropped entirely by `isPaintableImageSize`, a non-finite `lineHeight` falls back to the named style), and row content past 200 pages is clipped — user-visible behaviour changes that the originating issue's acceptance criteria never exercise and that reviewers of a list-indent fix are not primed to weigh.

The pagination change is recorded in the wrong canonical doc. `docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-row-splitting.md` is the subsystem doc for exactly the loop being modified (`packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts`, §1.1 split-point calculation) and it states the invariant "A split point is always *between* two atomic units inside a cell, never in the middle of one" plus the fallback "if the minimum is 0 … push the entire row to the next page". The new `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` clips content and forces a non-positive fragment up to `remaining`, contradicting both, yet the row-splitting doc (and `docs-pagination.md`) are untouched — the rationale was folded into `docs/design/docs/docs.md` instead, leaving two design docs disagreeing about how a tall row paginates.
searchedFor: grep MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN across the tree (diff only)
diff scan for edits to docs-pagination.md / docs-table-row-splitting.md

samples.summary: Duplicated ceiling: `MAX_FONT_SIZE = 400` restates `FONT_SIZE_MAX = 400` in `packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-catalog.ts:74`, and the comment openly says so rather than unifying. The frontend already imports the new bands from `@wafflebase/docs` (`yorkie-doc-store.ts`), so `font-catalog.ts` could have derived its picker max from the model band. Two definitions of "largest legal font size" in packages that depend on one another will drift: raise the picker's max and the model silently clamps every value the picker can now produce.

A third copy of the list-level ceiling survives the change: `listLevelAttr` hard-codes `Math.min(8, n)` / `Math.trunc(Number(...))` — the same [0, 8] band `normalizeListLevel` now owns. The change deduplicated the clipboard copy (`view/clipboard.ts` now imports `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`) but left the slides one, and slides already depends on `@wafflebase/docs`. The branch's own lessons file admits it (`docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-lessons.md:142`). Pre-existing, but this change is what created the canonical module to fold it into.

The paste sanitizer is the one producer of `rowHeights` / cell `padding` left with its own answer: `sanitizeTableData` still writes `asNumber(rawHeights[i])` (any finite number, including negatives and 1e9) instead of reusing `normalizeRowHeight`, and the change compensates by re-normalizing at layout time (`table-layout.ts` step 5b) plus bounding the paginator. Three places now decide what a legal row height is, and only two agree on the band — a pasted 1e9 height persists into the CRDT unaltered and is only masked at render, so the same document exported or read by a path that does not go through `computeTableLayout` sees the poisoned value.
searchedFor: grep normalizeRowHeight / normalizeRowHeights across the tree

samples.summary: One concept, three modules: the numeric bands for peer-writable attributes are split across `numeric-attrs.ts`, `row-height.ts`, and (for `listLevel`) `list-level.ts`, which also holds the unrelated gesture planner. The split is justified in comments by "a gesture plans with them", but the band and the planner are separable, and a future attribute has to guess which of the three files it belongs in (and remember three entry-point re-export lists plus the `entry-parity` allowlist).
